args.text:
Friday's big winter storm over the northeast of the United States knocked over a 227-year-old tree on the estate of the first US President, George Washington, at Mount Vernon in Virginia. As of yesterday, the mob running the Mount Vernon estate said the Canadian hemlock has been picked up to be kept and used for special projects.

The hemlock, planted in 1791, was blown over by gusts of reportedly up to 70 mph (about 110 km/h) on Friday.

Mount Vernon was Washington's own place, where he ran most of his two terms as president between 1789–1797 because the first White House wasn't finished yet. According to the Mount Vernon people, the hemlock is the best documented tree on the estate, sent by New York Governor George Clinton as a pressie delivered in a whisky barrel. The New York governor is no relation to the 42nd President, Bill Clinton, but George Clinton did later become the United States's Vice President under the Thomas Jefferson and James Madison governments between 1805–1812.

Other historic US trees that have come down lately include the seventh President Andrew Jackson's southern magnolia at the White House and the Pioneer Cabin giant sequoia in California's Calaveras Big Trees State Park, known for the car-sized tunnel cut through its trunk.
